title: Scikit-learn Preprocessing Quick Revision: Scaling, Encoding, Missing Values, Selection, Leakage, Pipelines
summary: Night-before revision of scikit-learn preprocessing: when and how to scale, encode categoricals, impute, select features, avoid data leakage, and wire it all into leak-proof Pipelines.

chapters.title: Preprocessing Mental Model and Scaling
points: Preprocessing turns raw columns into numeric model-ready features; every transformer has fit (learn stats from data) and transform (apply them)
StandardScaler: z = (x - mean) / std gives mean 0, std 1; no fixed range; sensitive to outliers
MinMaxScaler: x' = (x - min) / (max - min) maps to [0,1]; one outlier squashes all other values; use for bounded inputs like pixels or neural nets
RobustScaler uses median and IQR, so it resists outliers; scaling matters for distance/gradient models (KNN, SVM, linear/logistic with regularisation, PCA, neural nets) and not for tree models
Example: scaler = StandardScaler().fit(X_train); X_train_s = scaler.transform(X_train); X_test_s = scaler.transform(X_test), never fit on the test set

chapters.title: Encoding Categorical Features
points: OneHotEncoder makes one 0/1 column per category, for nominal data with no order; use handle_unknown='ignore' so unseen test categories do not crash
OrdinalEncoder maps categories to integers in a given order (categories=[['low','med','high']]); use only for truly ordered features
LabelEncoder is for the target y only, not for input features
Drop one dummy column (drop='first') for unregularised linear models to avoid the dummy-variable trap (perfect collinearity)
High-cardinality columns (thousands of levels) blow up one-hot width; use TargetEncoder (fitted inside CV to avoid leakage), frequency encoding or hashing instead

chapters.title: Handling Missing Values
points: Detect with df.isna().sum(); decide the pattern first: missing completely at random vs informative missingness
SimpleImputer(strategy='mean'|'median'|'most_frequent'|'constant', fill_value=...): median for skewed numerics, most_frequent for categoricals
Imputation statistics are learned on training data only, then reused on validation and test data
add_indicator=True appends a binary 'was missing' column, which keeps the signal when missingness is informative
KNNImputer fills from the k nearest rows and IterativeImputer models each feature from the others; both are slower and need scaled data; HistGradientBoosting handles NaN natively

chapters.title: Feature Selection Methods
points: Filter methods score features independently of the model: VarianceThreshold drops near-constant columns, SelectKBest(f_classif or mutual_info_classif, k=10) keeps the top k
Wrapper method RFE(estimator, n_features_to_select=k) repeatedly fits the model and drops the weakest feature; accurate but slow
Embedded methods select while training: L1/Lasso zeroes coefficients, SelectFromModel(RandomForest) thresholds on feature_importances_
Comparison: filter is fast and model-agnostic, wrapper is expensive and model-specific, embedded sits in between
Selection must be fitted on training folds only; selecting on the full dataset before CV inflates scores

chapters.title: Data Leakage and Scikit-learn Pipelines
points: Data leakage: information from the test set or the future gets into training, so the metric is optimistic and production performance collapses
Classic leaks: fitting scaler/imputer/selector on all data before splitting, target-derived features, duplicates across splits, and random splits on time series (use TimeSeriesSplit)
Pipeline([('prep', ct), ('model', clf)]).fit(X_train, y) refits every step on the training fold only, so cross_val_score(pipe, X, y, cv=5) is leak-free
ColumnTransformer([('num', num_pipe, num_cols), ('cat', OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore'), cat_cols)]) applies different preprocessing per column group; remainder='drop' by default
Tune with GridSearchCV(pipe, {'model__C': [0.1, 1, 10]}) using the step__param naming, and save the whole fitted pipeline with joblib.dump so serving applies identical preprocessing

chapters.title: Preprocessing Cheat Sheet
points: Scale: StandardScaler for general use, MinMaxScaler for bounded ranges, RobustScaler for outliers; trees do not need scaling
Encode: OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') for nominal, OrdinalEncoder for ordered, LabelEncoder only for y
Impute: SimpleImputer median for numeric, most_frequent for categorical, add_indicator=True when missingness is informative
Select: VarianceThreshold then SelectKBest (filter), RFE (wrapper), SelectFromModel or Lasso (embedded)
Golden rule: split first, then fit(train) and transform(train/test); put everything in Pipeline plus ColumnTransformer and cross-validate the whole pipeline
